title: Bridge spotlight prep and raw Q&A notes
content:
Purpose: quick bridge / spotlight notes + raw Q&A to carry into the 7-minute ops segment of the all-hands. This is my working pad not the final script. Keep it conversational, hit the numbers, and be ready to hand off to SRE if the question goes deep.

TL;DR (30s): We operated within our expanded capacity band over the last month; we saw a transient latency regression tied to a new batching heuristic rollout (rollout 2026-02-18) that affected ~3% of user traffic and was mitigated automatically by rollback. No customer-facing data was exposed; cost impact estimated ~0.9% MTD. Root cause summary and next steps below.

Opening (30-45s speaking bullets)
- Headline: "We had a short-lived latency regression after a heuristic change; we detected it quickly and reverted, and we have a concrete plan to prevent recurrence."
- Why this matters: reliability = developer trust; we prioritize fast recovery + transparency.
- What we did: alerting triggered, canary rollback, fast patch to the batching config, and widened canary thresholds.
- What we'll do next: two follow-up items (test harness + rollback hardening).

Key numbers to cite (simple soundbites)
- Affected traffic: ~3% peak; steady-state ~0.4% remaining in edge cases.
- Duration: peak regression window ~32 minutes; full mitigation ~1h 20m from detection to global rollback.
- Customer Impact: no authenticated calls failed; error tail rose from 0.02% to 0.35% during window.
- Cost: estimated +0.9% compute spend for the month if left unfixed; immediate incremental cost negligible due to autoscaling caps.

Known root cause (short):
- New dynamic batching heuristic mis-estimated token length distribution for a small set of long-sequence workloads. That led to suboptimal batch shapes and kernel selection path that amplified GPU context switch overhead.
- Secondary contributor: canary thresholds were too narrow (did not capture 95th-percentile latency for multi-tenant bursts).

Immediate remediation taken (chronological)
- Auto-alert flagged 95th latency deviation at 14:12 PST.
- Canary rollback triggered and validated by 14:44 PST.
- Team postmortem triage started; rollback config pinned in Dedicated pools.

Follow-up plan (owners + rough timeline)
- Short: (next 72h) Expand canary traffic ramp to include synthetic long-sequence load. Owner: Rowan Li.
- Medium: (2 weeks) Add batch-shape simulator into CI so kernel path decisions are exercised before canary. Owner: Eng-serving-runtime (PR scheduled).
- Long: (Q2) Expose a canary dashboard in Console showing distribution heatmaps and auto-fence policies. Owner: Product-console + Observability.

Proactive Q&A (short answers first)
Q: Did customer data leak?
A: No. This was a performance/latency regression only. No authentication or data-plane compromise.

Q: Which customers were affected?
A: Traffic distribution hit a subset of high-sequence internal test workloads and a handful of slow inference customers. We have outreach owners ready (CS ping list) and will notify any who saw sustained impact.

Q: Will this happen again?
A: We've already implemented immediate guardrails and scheduled CI changes; risk reduced. The long-term fix is to add batch-shape simulation to the CI and a canary-wide heatmap.

Tougher/prickly Qs (prep lines)
Q: Why did the canary not catch it?
A: Canary validations currently sample representative traffic but did not include extreme long-sequence synthetic variants. We're expanding the canary profile to cover the 99th percentile of sequence lengths for at-risk tenants. (See follow-up owner: Rowan)

Q: Could cost controls have prevented this?
A: Cost controls are orthogonal; the issue was misrouting into an inefficient kernel path. Cost controls would reduce spend but not the latency spike. New guardrails will include a runbook to quickly scale GPU worker counts for pathological batch shapes.

Q: Who made the change? Are we blaming someone?
A: We avoid person-level blame in public comms. This was a rollout decision with insufficient test coverage for an edge case. We'll present a blameless postmortem and concrete action items.

Live demo fallback / if we have a live console pull during the talk
- If Console is flaky or blocked: show anonymized heatmap (slideshow image 06) instead of live.
- If asked to show logs: have pre-saved gists and a short grep output prepared (linked in Slack thread).

Communication + outreach plan
- Internal: incident-summary + blameless triage doc (by EOD) -> #eng-ops + #prod-announce.
- Customer: CS will send templated reach-outs only to customers whose error rate >0.1% for >15m. Template owner: Maya Chen.
- Public: no public postmortem planned unless customer reach or broader impact; we will prepare a transparent timeline for any external requests.

Slides / artifacts to reference (file names)
- "Mar26_AllHands_Deck_v2.pdf" slide 5 (ops highlight)
- "canary-heatmap-2026-03-02.png" (for internal slide)
- Synthetic test harness PR: GH#1248 (branch: batch-sim)

Notes to self (very informal)
- DO: keep language simple; avoid kernel jargon beyond one sentence.
- DO: call out automation wins (alerting + rollback) — it's a positive outcome.
- DONT: promise a timeline for the CI cascade in public if not confirmed.
- DONT: use absolutes like "never" or "won't happen again". Use "reducing risk" phrasing.
- TODO: confirm the +0.9% cost calc with FinOps (Sahil) before live.

Unresolved / open questions for postmortem
- Which other rollout heuristics share the same kernel selector code path? (action: engineering riff-down)
- Can we make rollback fully automatic for that config? (action: release eng)

Micro-script for handing off to SRE lead (30s)
- "I'll cover what happened and the mitigation; Rowan, can you briefly explain the monitoring changes and what folks should expect next week?"

Slack prep message (post before segment)
- "Going live in 5m with a short ops update — highlights on a transient latency regression and fixes. If you're monitoring, please hold non-critical deploys for +30m after the all-hands. Link to incident doc: ENGOPS-4821"

Personal crib notes (for improvising)
- Keep it under 7 minutes. If pushed, cut the numbers and spend time on customer impact and next steps.
- Smile, thank team publicly for fast rollback.

End of scratchpad. This is still rough. Convert to a 3-bullet slide + 2 Qs for the finalized all-hands deck.
